summary: This is a clipped Snowflake documentation page for the ALTER SECURITY INTEGRATION command, which modifies the properties of an existing security integration. It gives the four syntax forms: SET parameters, UNSET a parameter, SET TAG, and UNSET TAG, with optional IF EXISTS. The page notes that syntax varies by security integration type and points to type-specific pages for details and examples.
one_line: Snowflake reference for the ALTER SECURITY INTEGRATION command, covering its SET/UNSET parameter and tag syntax forms.
key_facts: ALTER SECURITY INTEGRATION modifies the properties for an existing security integration.
The command syntax begins with ALTER [ SECURITY ] INTEGRATION [ IF EXISTS ] <name>.
One syntax form uses SET <parameters> to change properties of a named security integration.
One syntax form uses UNSET <parameter> to unset a parameter of a security integration.
A SET TAG form assigns tags as <tag_name> = '<tag_value>' pairs, separated by commas.
An UNSET TAG form removes one or more tags by <tag_name> from a security integration.
The IF EXISTS clause is optional in the SET and UNSET forms of the syntax.
The syntax varies considerably among security environments, meaning types of security integrations.
Specific syntax, usage notes, and examples are documented on separate type-specific pages referenced by the page.
The page sits under the Security category in a navigation path that also includes General, API, Catalog, External access, Notification and Storage.
The page header identifies the topic as SECURITY INTEGRATION.
